NHS Foundation Trust' decision located (Ms B Whitfield v Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, ET case 2301668/2022) is a different claimant surname coincidence against a different Trust, a first-instance Employment Tribunal (not EAT) decision, decided the following year, with an unrelated case number - it does not corroborate the seeded citation in any respect. The citation string itself is also internally inconsistent with real EAT citation practice: pre-2020 UKEAT decisions are cited 'UKEAT/NNNN/YY/(initials)' (e.g. UKEAT/0142/18/JOJ) and post-2020 EAT decisions (the format in force by 2021) are cited '[year] EAT number' (e.g. [2024] EAT 164), dropping the 'UKEAT' prefix entirely - a genuine 2021 EAT citation would not read '[2021] UKEAT ...'. The trailing '0142_21_0309' segment matches BAILII's internal file-slug convention for pre-2020 case numbers (caseNo_year_dayMonth), not a citation format, and case number 0142 in other years (0142/11, /17, /18, /19) all resolve to unrelated, real, differently-named cases (Oliver v The Ultimate Solution Partnership; Rawlinson v Brightside Group; Spaceman v ISS Mediclean; Inchcape Retail v Shelton) - reinforcing that '0142/21' is not this case's real number either. scripts/citation_lint.py's uk_neutral shape check matched a truncated '[2021] UKEAT 0142' fragment, confirming the operating-rules point that the linter is a shape check only and cannot itself confirm a citation is real.

name: NHS Manchester v Fecitt and others
date: 2011-10-19 (approx, per secondary sources - not independently pinpointed against BAILII's own date stamp this session)
pinpoint: UNKNOWN - not pinpointed to a specific paragraph this session
proposition: For ERA 1996 s.47B whistleblowing detriment, causation is satisfied where the protected disclosure materially influenced (more than trivially) the employer's treatment of the worker; the stricter 'in no sense whatsoever' EU-discrimination-derived test does not apply. On the co-worker point specifically: Fecitt (2011) itself held there was no vicarious liability under s.47B for detriment inflicted by a co-worker who committed no separate legal wrong, but that specific holding was legislatively superseded with effect from 25 June 2013 by ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E) (inserted by Enterprise and Regulatory Reform Act 2013 s.19), which now gives a worker a direct right of action against a co-worker or agent who subjects them to a s.47B detriment, treats that act as also done by the employer (vicarious liability), and gives the employer an 'all reasonable steps' defence. Fecitt's causation test ('materially influenced') remains good law; its co-worker/vicarious-liability point does not, for any detriment falling after 25 June 2013.
treatment: FOLLOWED (causation limb only; co-worker/vicarious-liability limb superseded by statute, see s.47B(1A)-(1E) note above)
primary_source_link: https://www.bailii.org (BAILII entry referenced by multiple independent secondary sources; direct BAILII fetch blocked by 403 in this session - existence and holding corroborated instead via Employment Cases Update, Croner-i, CMS Law-Now and Reed Smith commentary, which is independent-source corroboration under the OPERATING_RULES verification hierarchy but is SECONDARY, not a primary-source read, this session). The superseding statutory qualification itself (ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E)) WAS independently fetched and verified this session at https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1996/18/section/47B/2016-09-07 (in-force text) and cross-checked against the enacting provision https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2013/24/section/19/enacted - VERIFIED_PRIMARY_SOURCE for the qualification itself, distinct from the VERIFIED_SECONDARY_SOURCE tier that still applies to Fecitt's own holding.

name: Kuzel v Roche Products Ltd
proposition: In an ERA 1996 s.103A automatic unfair dismissal claim, the claimant must produce some evidence supporting the case that the protected disclosure was the reason for dismissal, but the legal burden never shifts to the claimant to prove that reason - it remains on the employer to show the reason (or principal reason) for dismissal, and if the employer's asserted reason is rejected, the tribunal must consider whether the true reason was the one alleged by the claimant.
primary_source_link: https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2008/380.html (URL located via search, page itself not fetched this session due to the same BAILII access restriction noted for AUTH-002; corroborated via Croner, Practical Law, and swarb.co.uk secondary summaries)

name: Beatt v Croydon Health Services NHS Trust
proposition: Where the making of a disclosure is the principal reason for dismissal, whether the disclosure was in fact protected (reasonable belief, public interest) is a question for the tribunal to determine objectively; the employer's own belief that the disclosure was not protected, or was not in good faith, is irrelevant to s.103A liability. Directly on point for ISS-003/ISS-004: this is itself an NHS whistleblowing dismissal case, real and correctly named, in contrast with the seeded fabricated authority.
primary_source_link: http://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2017/401.html (URL located via search; corroborated via 12 King's Bench Walk chambers note, Employment Cases Update, Croner-i, Bird & Bird)

name: Gallop v Newport City Council
proposition: An employer cannot simply 'rubber-stamp' an occupational health adviser's conclusion on disability status (or the s.15(2)/knowledge question for discrimination-arising-from-disability and reasonable-adjustments claims) - the employer must exercise its own judgement on the primary facts, including where OH has not been asked focused questions. Directly on point for ISS-005/ISS-006/ISS-007's employer-knowledge elements given the OH material in this matter's facts (F-015/F-016/F-022).
primary_source_link: http://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2013/1583.html (URL located via search; corroborated via Croner, Legal Island, Brightmine/HR & Compliance Centre)

name: Environment Agency v Rowan
date: 2008 (exact date UNKNOWN - not pinpointed this session)
proposition: A reasonable-adjustments claim under (now) Equality Act 2010 ss.20-21 requires the tribunal to first identify the specific PCP (or physical feature), the identity of any non-disabled comparators, and the nature/extent of the substantial disadvantage, before it can assess what adjustment(s) would have been reasonable. Directly on point for the ISS-007 gap already flagged in this matter (F-024: no specific PCP or adjustment yet identified in the facts supplied) - this authority explains why that gap is case-critical, not a drafting nicety.
primary_source_link: https://www.casemine.com/judgement/uk/5a8ff79d60d03e7f57eb02cc (EAT decision, persuasive rather than binding on itself but consistently applied since; not an official primary source - flagged as secondary)
